{{Quote|Admiral, we really need to do something about Fondor&hellip;|[[Darth Caedus]], to [[Cha Niathal]]|<ref name="Revelation" />}}
'''Fondor''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Freeworlds Territory]] of the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]], famous throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for its extensive orbital [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]], which were outclassed only by those at [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]]. The [[Fondor Shipyards/Legends|Shipyards]] were associated with the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and were vast enough to construct major flagships, such as the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]]. For many years, its capital city was [[Fondor City]], later succeeded by [[Oridin City]].

==Description==
Almost entirely industrialized, Fondor was an [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] surrounded by orbital shipyards and [[Drydock/Legends|drydocks]]. Its surface was almost totally covered with factories, cooling towers, and workers' barracks, as well as [[Mining/Legends|mine]] shafts leading deep into the planet's core and office complexes for the planet's ruling [[Fondor Guild of Starshipwrights|Guild of Starshipwrights]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

Fondor had a relatively small population of 5 billion around the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Most of the surface factories were autonomous, controlled by [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brains]] which oversaw billions of [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droids]].<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

==History==
===Early history===
[[File:Fondor_people.png|thumb|left|130px|Fondor administrator and zero-[[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] ship worker]]
Fondor was located in the [[Freeworlds Territory]] of the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]], a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] technically part of the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]], but so old and well-regarded that many considered it a part of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Lords of the Expanse">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref> The native [[Fondorian]]s were a [[Near-human|Near-Human]] species with no [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and [[Color/Legends|purple]] [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> The planet was completely industrialized eons ago. Its surface was scabbed with excavations, factories, cooling towers, steam tunnels, and offices, all related to the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] central role in [[Starship/Legends|starship]] construction. The planet also housed hectares of laborers' barracks for the dockworkers, many of whose jobs were above them.<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> Fondor was a main market for the [[Besadii/Legends|Besadii]] [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]].<ref name="Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref> The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] [[Mission to Fondor (Separatist Crisis)|mission to Fondor]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] foiled a scheme by [[Groodo]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] to destroy the Fondor Shipyards using a [[False Sun Runner|counterfeit]] ''[[Sun Runner]]'' [[Transport/Legends|transport]].<ref name="Star Wars Adventures 1: Hunt the Sun Runner">''[[Star Wars Adventures 1: Hunt the Sun Runner]]''</ref>

In [[3630 BBY]], a small colony of [[sleek]]s was discovered on a remote island of Fondor. These flightless [[Bird/Legends|birds]] were [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]] to extinction by the locals for the bird's delicious meat centuries ago.<ref name="Mission">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Bioanalysis|Get 'Em While They Last}}</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Fondor seceded to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], but the populace was generally unsupportive of the Separatist cause, and the planet contributed relatively little to the war effort.<ref name="The Essential Atlas" />

===The ''Executor'' project===
The contract to build the ''Executor'' came somewhat unexpectedly, as [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] was the manufacturer of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] and later instances of the ''Executor''-class. The Empire required complete secrecy in the project, closing off all nonmilitary traffic in the system. Though the dockyard bosses were angered by the fact that they could no longer serve their commercial clients, the fact that the project took up the majority of the yard's resources&mdash;and the legendary wrath of Vader&mdash;kept them in check.<ref name="TEGtPaM" /> Shortly before the Battle of Yavin an [[Invasion of Fondor|uprising]] was quickly suppressed by imperial forces.<ref name="EAWGG" /> Following the battle of Yavin, discontent deepened at the Fondor shipyards and in the surrounding colonies. Work slowdowns and acts of sabotage reached critical levels, threatening the tight timetable for completion of the Executor. Fearing retribution from [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself if delays persisted, the system’s governor reluctantly loosened some of the strict security protocols and improved conditions for workers, including granting greater benefits to [[Non-huMan|non-Human]] laborers. While these measures temporarily pacified the population, they also inadvertently allowed Rebel sympathizers and disloyal [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] to infiltrate the facility and carry out further sabotage.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>

In order to efficiently move ships, the Empire created a classified [[Hyperspace route/Legends|route]] linking Fondor with the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] world of [[Gandeal]]. The [[Gandeal-Fondor Hyperlane]] remained a well kept secret decades after its forging.<ref name="Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse" />
As an essential manufacturer of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], albeit unique variants, for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the shipyards became a target of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. In one instance, a [[Unidentified Executor-class Star Dreadnought|prototype Star Dreadnought]] fitted with a cloaking device underwent construction there. [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] penetrated the shipyards in stolen Imperial starfighters and terminated the project, preventing its completion.<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

===Regime change===
[[File:Fondor_Uprising.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The highly industrialized surface of Fondor]]In spite of its security, Fondor was seized by the [[Alliance of Free Planets]] very soon after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], giving the Alliance a key coreward shipyard and base. However, the supply of the raw materials that the shipyards demanded was briefly interrupted when Imperial [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Mordur]] persuaded [[Guild Master/Legends|Guildmaster]] [[Orrk]] to redirect [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm's]] strategic metal supplies from Fondor to himself&mdash;although [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] soon restored the situation and defeated the Admiral.<ref name="Star Wars 98: Supply and Demand">[[Star Wars (1977) 98|''Star Wars'' (1977) 98]]</ref> For decades, Fondor continued to supply the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] with [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and other [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]].<ref name="Exile (novel)">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref>

In [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], the planet also became a [[Battle of Fondor|target]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], though a blast from [[Centerpoint Station]] destroyed a portion of the enemy fleet, saving Fondor at the cost of the [[Hapan]] war fleet, which was also caught in the blast.<ref name="Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse" /> Fondor continued to supply the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] with starships in the war. The planet was eventually taken by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], but [[Battle at Fondor|retaken]] near the end of the war.<ref name="The Final Prophecy">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Final Prophecy]]''</ref>

===Second Galactic Civil War===
[[File:Fondor_TEA.jpg|thumb|Fondor]]
In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], it became allied with [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] in the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], as it had been chafing under GA military restrictions, and officially left the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="Exile (novel)" /> The planet's president at this time was [[Shas Vadde]].<ref name="Revelation" /> [[Darth Caedus|Joint Chief of State]] [[Darth Caedus]] planned to attack the planet in order to set an example for other rebellious worlds. It then became the scene of a [[Second Battle of Fondor|massive battle]] to retake it, with Caedus and his fleet bombarding [[Oridin City]] and other urban centers. [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Cha Niathal]] established the headquarters of her [[Alliance-in-exile|faction]] of the Galactic Alliance on the planet afterwards. When the Second Galactic Civil War ended with the defeat of the [[Confederation]], Fondor rejoined the Galactic Alliance.

In [[41 ABY]], the Imperial Remnant Head of State [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] was assassinated by the Sith [[Tahiri Veila]] over Fondor, after the former refused to support [[Darth Caedus]]'s faction of the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="Revelation" />

==Inhabitants==
The [[Near-Human]] [[Fondorian]]s made up 75% of Fondor's population, and were distinguished by their purple blood and lack of body hair. Fondorian society was [[Wikipedia:caste|caste]]-organized, with low-caste Fondorians traditionally having only one name. However, they might rise through society by gaining apprenticeships awarded by the [[Fondor Guild of Starshipwrights]] for generations of family service.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>
